[[File:Dr Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka.jpg|alt=A black woman, in a green dress, holding a book.|thumb|Dr Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka holding a copy of her memoir, "Walking with Gorillas: The Journey of an African Wildlife Vet", at the 2026 Kampala Writes Litfest where she was a speaker.]]
'''Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka''' (born 8 January 1970) is a [[Uganda]]n [[veterinarian]] and founder of [[Conservation Through Public Health]], an organisation dedicated to the coexistence of humans, endangered [[mountain gorillas]], and other animals in [[Africa]].<ref name="1R">{{cite web|date=31 July 2014
|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/uganda-bounces-back/index.html |title=How Uganda emerged from chaos to become a tourist destination once more |access-date=10 June 2018 | first=Joe |last=Yogerst |publisher=[[Cable News Network]] (CNN)}}</ref> She is also a trustee of [[The Gorilla Organization]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Trustee Reflects on Life "Walking with Gorillas" |url=https://gorillas.org/trustee-reflects-on-life-walking-with-gorillas/ |website=gorillas.org |publisher=The Gorilla Organization |access-date=2 January 2026 |date=7 Aug 2023}}</ref>

Kalema-Zikusoka was Uganda's first wildlife veterinary officer and featured in the [[BBC]] documentary ''Gladys the African Vet''.<ref name="2R">{{cite web|title=About Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka: Location: Uganda, 2010 Jury Member |access-date=10 June 2018 |publisher=The Rolex Awards for Enterprise |date=2010
|url=http://www.rolexawards.com/profiles/jury/gladys_kalema-zikusoka |author=The Rolex Awards}}</ref> In 2009, she won the [[Whitley Awards (UK)|Whitley Gold Award]] for her conservation work.<ref name="3R">{{cite web|access-date=10 June 2018 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2009/may/13/gorilla-protection-whitely-conservation-award |title=TV vet's scheme to protect gorillas in Uganda wins top conservation award | first=Sanjida |last=O'Connell |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] | date=13 May 2009 |location=London}}</ref> In December 2021, she was proclaimed a [[United Nations Environment Programme]]'s [[Champions of the Earth|Champion of the Earth]] for Science and Innovation for her work with the [[One Health]] initiative.<ref name="Vyawahare">{{cite news |last1=Vyawahare |first1=Malavika |title=Uganda's 'Dr. Gladys' honored by U.N. for work linking conservation and health |url=https://news.mongabay.com/2021/12/ugandas-dr-gladys-honored-by-u-n-for-work-linking-conservation-and-health/ |access-date=7 March 2022 |work=Mongabay Environmental News |date=13 December 2021}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
While growing up in [[Kampala]], Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka, at age 12, started a wildlife club at her school and organised trips to [[Queen Elizabeth National Park]].<ref name="4R">{{cite web|url=https://www.ctph.org/meet-the-team/ | title=Meet The Team: Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zukusoka, Founder and CEO |access-date=10 June 2018 |date=2017 |author=CTPH
|publisher=[[Conservation Through Public Health]] (CTPH) | location=Entebbe}}</ref> Her professional studies began when she won a scholarship to study at the [[University of London]] Royal Veterinary College, graduating with a [[Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine]]. In 2003, she obtained a [[Master of Veterinary Science|Master of Veterinary Medicine]] from [[North Carolina State University]]. She also holds a certificate in the management of non-profit organizations from [[Duke University]]. She earned a [[Master of Business Administration]] in 2016.<ref name="4R"/><ref>{{cite web|date=2003 |url=https://www.wcs-ahead.org/bios/bio_kalemazikusoka.html |title=IUCN 2003 World Parks Congress AHEAD Launch Forum: Biographies of Presenters: Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka, BVM, MVSc, Cert.NPM, CEO, Conservation Through Public Health |publisher=Animal & Human Health for the Environment And Development (AHEAD) |access-date=10 June 2018 | author=AHEAD |location=Ithaca, New York State |website=.wcs-ahead.org }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kalema-Zikusoka is married to Lawrence Zikusoka, a technology [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]] and one of the co-founders of Conservation Through Public Health. They have two children.<ref name="4R"/>

She is the daughter of the late political leader and women's rights advocate [[Rhoda Kalema]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Conservation Through Public Health — Protecting Gorillas Through One Health |url=https://ctph.org/ |access-date=2026-10-30 |website=Conservation Through Public Health |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional accomplishments==
In 1996, when Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka was 25, she was appointed the veterinary officer for the [[Uganda Wildlife Authority|Ugandan Wildlife Service]], which later merged with Uganda's national parks to become the Uganda Wildlife Authority. She was the first person to hold that position. At the time, [[Bwindi Impenetrable National Park|Bwindi]] gorillas numbered about 300. By 2018, the count had grown to approximately 460, moving the mountain gorilla from [[critically endangered]] status to [[Endangered species|endangered]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Britten |first=Fleur |date=28 April 2023 |title=A vet's life, fighting for the Bwindi mountain gorilla |pages=24 |work=[[The Guardian Weekly]]}}</ref> She pioneered the first wildlife translocation to restock Uganda's national parks following years of poaching during Uganda's civil wars.<ref name="5R"/>

As part of her veterinary research, she identified parasite transmission from humans to mountain [[Gorilla|gorillas]] as a significant risk factor for gorillas.<ref name="6R">{{cite journal| last1=Kalema-Zikusoka |first1=Gladys |last2=Rothman |first2=Jessica M. |last3=Fox |first3=Mark T. |date=January 2005 | title=Intestinal parasites and bacteria of mountain gorillas (Gorilla beringei beringei) in Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, Uganda |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=59–63 |issn=0032-8332 |journal=Primates; Journal of Primatology |pmid=15338419 |doi=10.1007/s10329-004-0103-y|s2cid=33668424 |url=http://researchonline.rvc.ac.uk/id/eprint/673/ |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Following her demonstration of pathways for human diseases to harm or kill gorillas, Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka, Lawrence Zikusoka, and Stephen Rubanga founded [[Conservation Through Public Health]] in 2003 to improve both human and [[Ecology|ecological]] health in Africa.<ref name="4R"/> CTPH is a non-profit organisation based in [[Uganda]] and the [[United States|USA]] that conducts programs that protect gorillas and other wildlife from human and [[livestock]] [[disease]] risk; that increase the local use of [[family planning]]; and that improve [[communication]] technologies to boost local development and to educate people about the environment. Kalema-Zikusoka is the CEO of the organisation.<ref name="4R"/>

In 2015, CTPH founded the award-winning social enterprise, Gorilla Conservation Coffee. Under this arrangement, the non-profit improves the livelihood of the surrounding community by assisting in getting international market prices for the community's [[Arabica coffee]] crop. With increased incomes, the community's illnesses and disease burden is reduced. Hence less disease is transferred to the resident gorillas. Also, a small fee is charged and retained by the farmers, whenever tourists traverse their gardens, when on gorilla treks through the community.<ref name="5R">{{cite web| url=https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/magazine/Saving-the-gorilla-with-quality-coffee-/434746-4727930-la6ylq/index.html |title=Saving the gorilla with quality coffee |access-date=25 August 2018 |date=25 August 2018
|newspaper=[[The EastAfrican]] |first=Rupi |last=Mangat |location=Nairobi}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==

Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka has received a number of honours, awards, and other public recognition of her environmental and humanitarian work. In 2009, she won the Whitley Gold Award, the top prize awarded in what has been considered the "[[Whitley Awards (UK)|Green Oscars]]".<ref name="3R" /> In 2008, the [[San Diego Zoo]] gave her its Conservation-in-Action Award.<ref name="4R" /> In 2006, Kalema-Zikusoka was elected to an [[Ashoka: Innovators for the Public|Ashoka Fellowship]].<ref name="7R">{{cite web| url=http://www.exploregreen.com/dr-gladys-kalema-zikusoka/ | title=About Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka |access-date=10 June 2018 |date=2013 |publisher=Exploregreen.com |location=St. Louis, Missouri |author=Exploregreen.com}}</ref> In 2007, [[Seed Magazine]] named her one of their eight Revolutionary Minds in Science.<ref name="7R" />

Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka was profiled in the BBC documentary ''Gladys the African Vet''. She has also been featured in documentaries by [[National Geographic]], Animal Planet, [[M-Net|MNet]] and [[Uganda Broadcasting Corporation|Uganda Television]]. She was chosen among nine international environmental leaders to write a letter to the next [[United States|US]] president in ''[[Sierra Club]]'' magazine, November/December 2008 issue.<ref name="7R"/>

In 2018, Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka was awarded the EarthCare Award by the [[United States]]-based [[Sierra Club]], in recognition of her "unique contribution to international environmental protection and conservation", as related to her work in environmental protection and co-existence between communities and mountain gorillas in [[Uganda]]. She received the award on 29 September 2018, at a ceremony held in [[Denver]], [[Colorado]], United States.<ref name="9R">{{cite web| url=https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/magazine/Ugandan-wildlife-vet-gets-coveted-Sierra-Club-award/434746-4813808-hp1ul4z/index.html |title=Ugandan wildlife vet gets coveted Sierra Club award |access-date=20 October 2018 |date=20 October 2018 |newspaper=[[The EastAfrican]] |first=Bamuturaki | last=Musinguzi |location=Nairobi}}</ref>

In December 2021, she was proclaimed the [[United Nations Environment Programme]]'s [[Champions of the Earth|Champion of the Earth]] for Science and Innovation.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Environment |first1=U. N. |title=Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka |url=https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/laureates/2021/gladys-kalema |website=Champions of the Earth |access-date=4 January 2022 |language=en |date=3 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Champions of the Earth: The Ugandan vet protecting people and wildlife |url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2021/12/1108252 |website=UN News |access-date=4 January 2022 |language=en |date=21 December 2021}}</ref>

In April 2022, Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka was awarded the [[Edinburgh Medal]]<ref>[https://www.sciencefestival.co.uk/event-details/edinburgh-medal-address-conservation-and-one-health 2022] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331112507/https://www.sciencefestival.co.uk/event-details/edinburgh-medal-address-conservation-and-one-health |date=31 March 2023 }}</ref> for her work improving the quality of life of people and wildlife to enable them to coexist in and around protected areas in Africa. She is a pioneer in community-led 'one health' approaches to conservation exploring and supporting the delicate interplay between humans and wildlife.

In November 2023, Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka was named to the [[BBC]]'s [[100 Women (BBC)|100 Women]] list as one of the world's inspiring and influential women.<ref name=BBC>{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2023 |title=BBC 100 Women 2023: Who is on the list this year? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/resources/idt-02d9060e-15dc-426c-bfe0-86a6437e5234 |access-date=2023-11-24 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> Silverback 10 Award — Uganda Tourism Association. 2024, Ekkula Sustainable Tourism Awards — Woman Champion of Sustainable Tourism, 2024 African Primatological Society — Lifetime Achievement Award, 2024, President's Mammal Society Award, UK.

Featured on 3 Oct 2026 (Full Episode) Africa Earth’s Wild Home presented by ROLEX and National Geographic. Narrated and executive produced by Academy Award nominee Wunmi Mosaku.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC UNVEILS AFRICA EARTH'S WILD HOME, THE FIRST SEASON OF A NEW MULTIYEAR NATURAL HISTORY FRANCHISE AND ONE OF THE MOST AMBITIOUS SERIES ABOUT AFRICA EVER PRODUCED |url=https://www.detpress.com/natgeo/pressrelease/national-geographic-unveils-africa-earths-wild-home-the-first-season-of-a-new-multiyear-natural-history-franchise-and-one-of-the-most-ambitious-series-about-africa-ever-produced/ |access-date=2026-10-30 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Dr. Gladys was nominated for 2027 Indianapolis Prize and is CNN Hero for 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Atukunda |first=Rogers |date=2026-10-29 |title=Ugandan Wildlife Veterinarian Dr Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka Named Among Top 5 CNN Heroes of 2026 |url=https://softpower.ug/ugandan-veterinarian-gladys-kalema-zikusugandan-wildlife-veterinarian-dr-gladys-kalema-zikusoka-named-among-top-5-cnn-heroes-of-2026oka-named-among-top-5-cnn-heroes-of-2026/ |access-date=2026-10-30 |website=SoftPower News |language=en-US}}</ref>
